title: Superconducting parametric amplifiers based on arrays of unequal Josephson junction elements
authors: Boris Chesca, Tom Dixon, Narendra Acharya, Renuka D. Pothuraju, Jacob W. Dunstan, Connor D. Shelly, Oscar W. Kennedy
abstract: Impedance matching is a crucial feature of an amplifier used to increase its instantaneous bandwidth and is typically achieved using static LC resonators. Here we show an approach to impedance matching in parametric amplifiers using arrays of unequal Josephson-junction-based elements (rf/dc SQUIDs, SNAILs, etc). The elements act either as small-footprint flux-tunable inductors forming an impedance-matching circuit, or 'active' amplifier elements which result in amplifier gain. We develop an analytical theory describing these systems, predicting a quasi-non-periodic amplifier frequency and gain modulation with applied flux and the broadening of gain bandwidths. We demonstrate this in devices using arrays of flux-focused SNAILs where flux biasing varies across the array. We find instantaneous bandwidths of 200 MHz with $>$17 dB of gain centred at $\sim$5.4 GHz in a device without a static impedance matcher. This broadening of amplifier bandwidth is stable with $>$100 MHz bandwidth at 17 dB gain across $>$1.2 GHz tunable bandwidth. Our analytical model captures flux dependence and qualitatively reproduces gain-bandwidths giving confidence in our understanding of these systems and allowing operational figures of merit to be optimised in future devices.
summary: This paper proposes a novel method for enhancing the bandwidth of superconducting parametric amplifiers by utilizing arrays composed of Josephson junctions with unequal physical properties. By exploiting the resulting quasi-non-periodic flux dependence, the impedance matching function is integrated into the device itself, achieving high gain over significantly broadened bandwidths without external matching circuits.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of achieving impedance matching in superconducting parametric amplifiers (JPAs) to increase their instantaneous bandwidth, moving beyond traditional static LC resonators.
main_result: Using arrays of unequal Josephson junction elements allows the impedance matching function to be integrated directly into the amplifier structure, yielding stable, broad bandwidths (e.g., 200 MHz bandwidth at 17 dB gain) without external matching circuits.
method: The authors developed an analytical theory by modeling the system using a multi-dimensional potential energy function derived from arrays of unequal Josephson junctions, which was then analyzed semi-classically.
model_or_system: The system consists of parametric amplifiers based on arrays of unequal Josephson junction elements (like SNAILs). The physics is governed by a complex potential energy function $U_{	ext{array}}$ that exhibits quasi-non-periodic flux dependence due to the unequal junction elements.
key_observables: Instantaneous bandwidth, amplifier gain ($>17$ dB), quasi-non-periodic flux dependence of inductance and gain, and effective three-wave mixing interaction strength ($\left|g_{3\alpha p,eff}ight|^2$).
important_parameters: External magnetic flux ($\Phi_{	ext{ext}}$), Josephson junction parameters ($E_J, E_C$), and the flux-focusing ratios ($R_k$) characterizing the inequality of the junctions.
main_assumptions: Approximations include neglecting geometric inductance ($ eta_S \ll 1$) and assuming specific relationships between junction energies ($E_{J,k} \gg E_{C,J}$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematics of the unequal junction arrays, heatmaps of the multi-dimensional potential confirming unsynchronized operation, and plots showing the flux dependence of the effective gain terms compared to identical junction arrays.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the fundamental Hamiltonian description of the array potential, develops the analytical theory for the non-linear inductance and gain coefficients, and culminates in demonstrating the superior bandwidth performance achieved by exploiting the quasi-non-periodic nature of unequal junctions.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems because it deals with enhancing the performance (bandwidth) of a quantum nonlinear device (the JPA) by engineering the underlying physical coupling mechanism (the junction array inhomogeneity) rather than relying on external classical components.
